candidates.printedLatin: Quid enim est dicere esse genus peccati de quo homo possit veniam consequi?
candidates.englishAsRendered: For what is it to say that there is a kind of sin for which a man may [not] obtain pardon?
candidates.conjecture: Quid enim est dicere esse genus peccati de quo homo non possit veniam consequi?
candidates.whyContradiction: The sentence sits inside Richard's summary of Augustine's Retractationes, which argues that of no one, however wicked, is one to despair ("de quocunque pessimo in hac vita constituto non est desperandum"), and the very next clause glosses this rhetorical question as teaching a man 'to despair' ("quid, inquam, aliud est hoc dicere quam ejusmodi hominem docere ut desperet") and links it to Cain's despairing cry. Without non, the printed clause asserts the opposite of the point being illustrated: that there IS a kind of sin from which a man CAN obtain pardon would not teach despair at all. Only 'cannot obtain pardon' produces the despair the following sentence names.
candidates.note: Not listed in any cruces.md for this work (11543 has no cruces.md at all). Worth flagging: the underlying TEI source (sources/pl/tei/11543.xml, line 216) already prints the word bracketed as '[non]', i.e. a prior editorial hand had already silently supplied the dropped negative before this translation was made; our English rendering correctly follows that supplied reading. So the defect itself is genuine and matches the sweep's target pattern exactly, but its correction predates this project.
